title: I Asked AI to Help Me Beat the Stock Market
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Self-promotional: Chris presents his own free, email-gated stock tool. No paid sponsor is identified in the cleaned transcript.

stated_problem.quote: How can I use AI and AI vibe coding tools to help me develop a stock investing strategy so I can beat the market without risking my family's financial future?
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Neil Stocks
idea.one_liner: A free, email-gated web tool for self-directed investors to filter stocks by network effects and founder leadership, then compare historical portfolio returns with the S&P 500.
idea.offer: A stock research and portfolio comparison tool with filters, historical data, charts, and backtested returns.
idea.revenue_model: Free access behind email signup; no monetization is stated, though the speaker mentions possibly building more features later.

key_quotes.quote: Called Neil Stocks, NEL, Network Effects, Founderled.
So at the end of the day to see the final product, this probably took 45 minutes of prompting.
The S&P has returned 9% over this time frame weighted and 12% unweed and this portfolio would have returned 22.4%.
I put this free website behind an email form. So, if you want to use it for free, it's completely free.

claims.claim: The initial research screen returned 26 S&P 500 companies meeting the network-effects and founder-led criteria.
claims.quote: Find me all of the companies in the S&P 500 that have both network effects and are still founderled. There were 26 of them.

claims.claim: The comparison modeled $100 investments in each selected company and the S&P 500 on the companies’ IPO dates.
claims.quote: So one scenario is $100 in each of the 26 companies and the other scenario is $100 in the S&P 500 on the same day that each of those companies went public.

claims.claim: The speaker described the modeled portfolio as a $2,600 investment.
claims.quote: So then I can track over time how much money would I have today because really we're talking about investing $2,600.

claims.claim: The requested chart covered performance from one day through 20 years.
claims.quote: I want to see one day, one week, one month, one year, 5year, 10 year, 20-year performance in a sleek chart like Robin Hood shows.

claims.claim: The data table included how many shares would be needed for a $100 purchase.
claims.quote: You can see the name of the company, the ticker, the IPO price, how many shares you would need to buy $100 worth, today's price, and if you look at the formula right here, I'm just using the Google Finance formula.

claims.claim: Google Finance data in the sheet refreshed every minute or two.
claims.quote: So, this updates every minute or two.

claims.claim: The company scoring prompt used a 1-to-10 scale for network effects.
claims.quote: And so over here I had a prompt that said tell me on a scale of 1 to 10 and then I inserted the name of the company how much in this case Kagra Brands enjoys network effects.

claims.claim: The GPT for Sheets credits cost about $15.
claims.quote: It cost me like 15 bucks in credits and I got this sliding scale of how much a company has network effects and how much they are founder led or not.

claims.claim: The app used the whole S&P 500 dataset.
claims.quote: Here's the whole S&P 500. Here's what each of the columns mean.

claims.claim: The speaker described filters using a five-plus network-effects score and founder scores of eight-plus or five-plus.
claims.quote: I also wanted to see like should I invest in companies that have a five plus network effect score only 8 plus 5 plus founder etc.

claims.claim: The speaker gave a hypothetical comparison between stocks meeting the criteria from 10 and 15 years earlier.
claims.quote: Let's say I invested in one stock that fits these criteria 10 years ago and one that fits it 15 years ago.

claims.claim: The speaker requested percentages formatted to one decimal place.
claims.quote: I only want one decimal point on my percentages.

claims.claim: The build took about 45 minutes of prompting.
claims.quote: So at the end of the day to see the final product, this probably took 45 minutes of prompting.

claims.claim: The demonstrated filter selected scores from 8 to 10 for network effects and founder leadership.
claims.quote: And if I rank it, let's go 8 to 10 on network effects, 8 to 10 on founder.

claims.claim: The default time horizon was 10 years.
claims.quote: The default is a 10-year time horizon.

claims.claim: Six companies matched the displayed filters.
claims.quote: You can see right here, six companies match your filters.

claims.claim: Five of the six matches had valid IPO price data.
claims.quote: Five of those six have valid IPO price data because some of them I just wasn't able to get all the data for.

claims.claim: The backtest showed weighted S&P returns of 9%, unweighted S&P returns of 12%, and a portfolio return of 22.4%.
claims.quote: The S&P has returned 9% over this time frame weighted and 12% unweed and this portfolio would have returned 22.4%.

claims.claim: The speaker said the displayed portfolio return was over twice the weighted S&P return.
claims.quote: Which is over twice the weighted return.

claims.claim: Use of the website was free.
claims.quote: So, if you want to use it for free, it's completely free.

claims.claim: The speaker said there was nothing to pay for.
claims.quote: So, if you want to use it for free, it's completely free. There's nothing to pay for.

ideas.delivery: Chris built a self-serve web app in Replit, connected it to a live Google Sheet for stock data, and gates access through an email form. Users view filters and historical return comparisons in the app.

prices: $100 hypothetical investment per company and S&P comparison
